summary: Preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload in eslint stub package
details: The package advertises itself as an ESLint processors stub — dist/index.js is a 15-line file exporting inert preprocess/postprocess handlers. Its package.json declares scripts.preinstall = "node setup.mjs". setup.mjs probes for a local bun binary; if none is present it downloads a Bun runtime archive from github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases, extracts bun/bun.exe into an OS tmpdir, chmods it executable, then invokes it against the sibling math_init.js bundled in the tarball. math_init.js is a ~727 KB Bun-compiled CJS bundle (header // @bun @bun-cjs) with obfuscator-style hex identifiers (_0xXXXX), a shuffled constant array (n7gIxM=[0x0,0x1,...]), and an array-rotation decoder (WV8StW). The payload is executable only by the just-downloaded Bun runtime, hiding its behavior from Node-based static review. A trivial ESLint processor stub has no legitimate need for a second language runtime or a 727 KB obfuscated blob, and the scope @servicetitan is consistent with a namespace-hijack or typosquat drop. Installing the package via `npm install` automatically fetches a foreign runtime and runs opaque attacker-controlled code on the installer's machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
